summary: The Global Korea Scholarship brings international students to Korea for a master's or PhD on a full government award, run by NIIED. You apply either through the Korean embassy in your country or directly to a designated Korean university, and many scholars begin with a year of Korean language training.
meta_description: Korea's GKS pays tuition, airfare, a monthly allowance and Korean lessons for a master's or PhD. Embassy and university tracks, eligibility and deadlines.
covers: Full tuition at your Korean university.
Return airfare, a monthly living allowance and a settlement allowance on arrival.
Up to one year of Korean language training if you need it.
eligibility: Citizens of the countries NIIED invites that year, applying through the embassy or university track.
Under 40 on 1 September of the year you start.
A bachelor's degree (for a master's) or a master's degree (for a PhD) by 31 July of that year.
A cumulative grade point average of at least 2.64 out of 4.0, or the equivalent on other scales (2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5, 3.23/5.0).
how_to_apply: Choose one track: the embassy track in your country or the university track with a designated Korean university.
On the embassy track you may pick up to three universities, and at least one must be a regional (Type B) university.
Apply online on the Study in Korea site during the application window (12–25 February in 2026).
Pass the first screening, then university admission; you are selected only if a university admits you.
watch_out: You can apply on one track only; applying on both disqualifies you.
Each country has its own quota, so the number of places differs from country to country.
The amounts are set in NIIED's guidelines each year, so check the current guidelines before you budget.

sources.title: Embassy of Korea in India: 2026 GKS for graduate degrees
